- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.7 for 3+ consecutive days), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 5–10 day horizons.
- Mean reversion is triggered when price drops >10% from recent peak; model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average if drop exceeds 8%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating +/–), model exhibits erratic behavior; use median of last 5–7 days as baseline for smoothing.
